# PRIMA-NEXT complete file reference

Prepared on 7 October 2026. Start with [the project explanation](PROJECT_EXPLAINED.md). This reference covers every discoverable Python source file, including package initializers, tests, upstream source, and the non-Python executable files listed below.

**Coverage:** 385 project-owned Python files (44,720 lines), 53 upstream Python files. Files in environments, Git internals and generated bytecode/caches are excluded. The notebook has its own section-by-section coverage.

**How this was checked:** source text was parsed for every Python file. Definitions/docstrings, test cases and local imports are recorded in [the JSON inventory](project-source-inventory.json); important runtime, storage, retrieval, affect, tool and benchmark flows were additionally traced in source. This is a file-level explanation with deeper analysis of the main flows, not a claim of line-by-line formal verification or dynamic execution of every branch.

**Role labels are conservative static evidence.** Imports inside functions and package exports are included, so the runtime closure can contain optional/evaluator helpers that never execute in a canonical request. An imported class is not proof of activation. `runtime/route_profiles.py`, controller call sites, diagnostics and route tests establish actual execution. Dynamic/external callers can exist outside this scan.

**Improvement notes:** each entry has a specific next step or its subsystem recommendation. A recommendation is not a newly reproduced bug unless the project explanation identifies it as such. Do not rewrite all files simply because they appear here.

## Reading map

Read the project explanation first. For a request lifecycle, search this reference for `runtime/contracts.py`, `runtime/route_profiles.py`, `runtime/prima_runtime.py`, then `workflow/orchestration_engine.py`. For quality problems, follow retrieval, reasoning, generation, then the benchmark evaluator. For retained information, follow note/repository/index, admission, supervisor and evolution. The tests section names the observable behaviors already protected. Each file is a separate searchable heading.

## root: Entrypoint

**Why this area exists:** A tiny executable entry makes the affect subsystem inspectable.

### [main.py](../main.py)

**Purpose:** Runs a small interactive affect classifier demo, printing typed emotion/PAD updates; it does not launch the full agent workflow.

**Role:** Standalone/export utility or script; no resolved owned importer found. This is not proof it can be deleted. **Size:** 24 lines.

**Main pieces:**

- `main` (line 10): The named implementation/record used by the purpose above.

**Uses project files:** [affect/__init__.py](../affect/__init__.py).

**Improve when needed:** Keep the demo honest about its scope; use PrimaRuntime for end-to-end agent scenarios.

## Upstream Python: every checked-out file

The three `external` directories are Git submodules. Dataset JSON may be consumed by PRIMA loaders, but these original neural trainers, browser/operator runners and dataset patchers are not thereby part of canonical inference. None of the owned resolved Python import edges imports a module through `external`; scripts/manual usage remain possible. The upstream source is included individually so it is not silently omitted from this explanation.

Upstream recommendations: retain pinned revisions/licenses and identify the selected dataset variant/hash. Do not run dataset-changing scripts or replace gold answers to improve a score. Modify upstream code only for a specific upstream task, with its own instructions/tests. Local `AGENTS.md` files in toolkit directories govern work there, not PRIMA runtime routes.

## Kaggle notebook: every executable section

[PRIMA_Kaggle_Benchmark.ipynb](../PRIMA_Kaggle_Benchmark.ipynb) is the deploy/run/report notebook. It has 19 executable cells and 20 Markdown cells. It orchestrates the existing native campaign helpers; it is not another evaluator.

| Section / code-cell index (zero-based) | Purpose and why it exists | Improvement / acceptance boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Global configuration / 2 | Defines session clock, selected benchmark, model/dataset pins, smoke/full flags and resource budgets. | Keep one frozen effective identity; changing configuration invalidates timing/resume. |
| Benchmark selector / 4 | Validates early guards and resolves the one selected benchmark and output namespace. | Fail before warmup for unsupported topology/guards; avoid opening unrelated inputs. |
| Hardware inspection / 6 | Records Python/OS/RAM/disk/GPU state and supplies checked subprocess helpers. | Report measured hardware; synthetic checks are not a hardware pass. |
| Repository setup / 8 | Clones/fetches the recorded branch, rejects source drift and installs the selected dependency set. | Keep source identity clean; do not discard local changes or claim an older branch has new helpers. |
| Ollama setup / 10 | Starts/reuses provider processes and cached pinned model resources; smoke avoids model downloads. | Verify endpoint/model digests and cleanup; preserve cache identity and resource guards. |
| Exact-context GPU preflight / 12 | Warms inference and verifies actual context and GPU residency, including replica placement when selected. | Do not lower context/offload to bypass failed requirements; qualify actual topology. |
| Dataset validation / 14 | Finds the selected input and freezes/validates hashes, native schema, splits and coverage. | Require unambiguous source selection; do not equate a chosen file with complete trusted data. |
| Campaign configuration / 16 | Constructs typed native campaign payloads for canary, pilot and full execution. | Keep smoke isolated/partial and profiles/budgets aligned with runtime diagnostics. |
| Canary and tiny/representative pilot / 18 | Runs native campaigns with live monitoring, stage artifacts, equality/overlap checks and timing estimates. | Measure each benchmark afresh; do not credit theoretical concurrency speedups. |
| Measured full-run gate / 20 | Requires explicit full enablement plus current identity, coverage, resources and session-time admission. | Preserve the 10.5-hour campaign/12-hour session gates and elapsed setup/artifact reserve. |
| Native evaluation / 22 | Loads native manifests, summaries and task-specific metrics without inventing notebook scoring. | Incomplete child output is not a complete source evaluation. |
| Architecture diagnostics / 24 | Reconciles planned/executed components, calls/results, corrections and skipped responsibilities. | Task-unselected means not applicable; selection is not execution. |
| Performance/resources / 26 | Computes checkpoint latencies/tokens/throughput and sampled RAM/GPU peaks. | Sampled peaks can miss spikes; overlapping provider sums are not campaign wall time. |
| Error/failure analysis / 28 | Builds stable-ID lists for runtime failures, wrong answers, misses, abstentions and correction outcomes. | Keep execution errors distinct from valid but incorrect answers and metric failures. |
| Human-readable report / 30 | Writes consolidated reports/effective artifacts while preserving native provenance. | Avoid baseline-gain claims without valid paired experiments. |
| Result visualization / 32 | Plots stored metrics and measured costs with benchmark-specific panels. | Label denominators/partial scope; reuse stored evaluation rather than rescore for plots. |
| Artifact validation / 34 | Checks statuses, IDs, hashes, metric/file schemas, credential patterns and full-source reconciliation. | Failures remain partial; exact completeness is a launch/report boundary. |
| Packaging / 36 | Builds the session output archive, validates package/identity and records its checksum. | Exclude models/datasets/cache/repository; retain time for validation and a recoverable partial package. |
| Download / 38 | Displays the resulting archive path/checksum and download link. | Use the validated archive identity; download availability alone is not success. |

## Setup, CI, configuration and executable resources

These files influence executed behavior even when they are configuration/data rather than Python source.

| File | Purpose | Improvement / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| [setup.ps1](../setup.ps1) | Checks/selects Python 3.14, creates/reuses .venv, installs requirements, initializes submodules and copies the example environment only if absent. | Separate optional installs only when installation cost matters; review the deletion of an incompatible .venv before extending setup. |
| [.github/workflows/ci.yml](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) | Runs repository quality gates on hosted Python 3.14: capability report, compile, pytest, Ruff, Xenon, mypy and Bandit. | Keep checks comparable locally/CI; real model quality and GPU readiness require additional real experiments. |
| [pyproject.toml](../pyproject.toml) | Configures test discovery, Ruff lint rules, baseline/strict mypy scope and third-party typing exceptions. | Retire exceptions with measured typed boundary work; keep exclusions honest and discoverable. |
| [requirements.txt](../requirements.txt) | Lists runtime, benchmarks, training, semantic metrics and pinned developer tools for the full local research environment. | Capture a resolved experiment environment; broad runtime minimum versions alone do not freeze reproducibility. |
| [requirements-kaggle.txt](../requirements-kaggle.txt) | Provides a smaller native Ollama/stable-embedding/legacy-affect/lexical-reranker dependency set for the default notebook path. | Use the full list for explicitly selected encoder/HF/BERTScore features and record actual installed versions. |
| [.env.example](../.env.example) | Documents example legacy/runtime paths and switches without real secret values. | Audit every setting against a live reader: model/provider examples and canonical PRIMA_EMBEDDING_BACKEND settings are currently incomplete here. |
| [config/retrieval.yaml](../config/retrieval.yaml) | Sets dense/sparse/temporal/graph fusion weights: 0.40/0.30/0.15/0.15. | Tune on development retrieval, freeze for final evaluation and record effective values. |
| [config/memory_importance.yaml](../config/memory_importance.yaml) | Sets admission threshold 0.55 and novelty/emotion/relevance/recurrence/reflection weights. | Measure useful retention versus storage growth; freeze thresholds before evaluation. |
| [benchmarks/campaign/smoke.yaml](../benchmarks/campaign/smoke.yaml) | Defines the tiny fake-provider campaign used for deterministic local three-benchmark wiring and resume checks. | Label fixture/fake output clearly; it is separate from the notebook real-provider smoke. |
| [benchmarks/campaign/full_gpu.example.yaml](../benchmarks/campaign/full_gpu.example.yaml) | Provides a deployment-specific full GPU campaign template with fields that preflight must resolve. | Do not infer missing identities/endpoints/resources; qualify the supplied real environment. |
| [bandit.yaml](../bandit.yaml) | Configures static security scanning exclusions for environments/tests/upstream areas. | Check exclusions explicitly; scanner success does not establish policy isolation. |
| [.gitmodules](../.gitmodules) | Pins three upstream repository locations for LoCoMo, corrected LoCoMo v2 and HotpotQA checkouts. | Record selected submodule revisions and dataset hashes; upstream website/tooling presence is not runtime usage. |
| [.gitignore](../.gitignore) | Keeps generated caches, environments and output artifacts out of authored version-controlled source. | Retain intentional experiment manifests/results separately; avoid accidentally committing secrets or model weights. |
| [.github/CODEOWNERS](../.github/CODEOWNERS) | Identifies review owners for repository areas; does not change runtime behavior. | Update ownership as actual maintainers change. |
| [memory/retrieval/resources/intent_patterns.json](../memory/retrieval/resources/intent_patterns.json) | Data-driven lexical intent patterns consumed by QueryAnalyzer. | Treat rule edits as retrieval changes; verify paraphrases and freeze resource identity. |
| [memory/retrieval/resources/lexical_expansions.json](../memory/retrieval/resources/lexical_expansions.json) | Data-driven lexical query expansions consumed by QueryAnalyzer. | Measure candidate recall and query drift; avoid benchmark-answer-specific terms. |
| [memory/retrieval/resources/relation_expansions.json](../memory/retrieval/resources/relation_expansions.json) | Relation expansion vocabulary for deterministic rewriting. | Evaluate general relation support, not memorized gold phrasing. |
| [memory/retrieval/resources/temporal_patterns.json](../memory/retrieval/resources/temporal_patterns.json) | Patterns/operators for extracting temporal constraints. | Test relative/ambiguous dates and use explicit provenance/reference time. |

## Data, documentation, licenses and installed dependencies

Evaluation JSON/TSV fixtures and gold datasets are inputs, not authored algorithms. Synthetic profiles and labels are explained through their loaders/generators/evaluators above. The evaluation dataset files include inputs_100, emotion_gold, reflection_gold, retrieval_gold and retrieval_gold_v2; GoEmotions test fixtures provide tiny train/dev/test TSV splits and label names; locomo_smoke.json is explicitly a small fallback fixture. Full upstream JSON variants can differ in questions/captions/evidence: freeze the actual selected file/hash rather than infer equivalence from its name.

README.md states research scope/setup. The architecture ADR states ownership rules. The truth matrix and RELEASE_READINESS are dated implementation evidence. Reasoning docs include historical paths; benchmark RUNBOOK and RESULT_CLAIM_POLICY define operations and reporting. The October Kaggle plan/smoke/session-budget/reference notes describe the current operational objective and recorded measurements. LICENSE/NOTICE/CONTRIBUTORS/.mailmap record project license, acknowledgments and contributor attribution; upstream licenses remain independent.

Installed library source, binary/model weights, generated logs/results/cache/bytecode, diagrams, images, videos and source maps are not first-party executable logic. Their roles are storage/vector search (Chroma/NumPy), graph operations (NetworkX), embeddings/encoders/training (sentence-transformers/PyTorch/Transformers), validation/settings (Pydantic), transport (requests/urllib), language features (spaCy/NLTK), metrics/plots (BERTScore/matplotlib/scikit-learn), resource telemetry (psutil), YAML configuration and developer tooling. Recommendations here reuse those installed capabilities; no additional dependency was introduced.

## Coverage check

The generator verified one entry for each of the 385 owned Python paths and explicitly listed all 53 upstream Python paths. All 19 notebook code cells parsed successfully. Every discovered .ps1/.sh/.js/.html/.css path is listed above; executable CI and behavior-affecting configuration/resources are listed separately. Empty initializers are included. Source hashes/definitions/importers/test-case names are available in the JSON inventory. This scope does not claim third-party package internals or hidden deployment-specific code were reviewed.
